excerpt: "Scientists have discovered that the words we choose — whether in stories, tweets, or conversation — lean heavily toward safety over danger. This hidden bias, found by analyzing billions of words, could change how we study language and teach computers to understand us."

title: "How can invisible magnetic whirlpools help computers think like brains?"

title: "Why does our Moon have two very different faces — and how did Chang'e 6 help solve the mystery?"
excerpt: "Our Moon looks different depending on which side you view it from. The near side is covered in dark smooth plains, while the far side is bright and heavily cratered. title: "What happens when a mushroom makes you see tiny humans walking on your dinner plate?"
excerpt: "In parts of China and the Philippines, people eat a special wild mushroom called Lanmaoa asiatica for its savory flavor — but if it isn't cooked long enough, they start seeing dozens of tiny human figures climbing on their food, walking around furniture, and even swimming in their soup. title: "NASA's Swift Space Observatory Completes a 22-Year Mission Spotting the Universe's Brightest Explosions"

title: "How did NASA's OSIRIS-REx asteroid mission find organic building blocks from the dawn of the solar system?"

title: "What did Parker Solar Probe discover about the Sun's twisted magnetic braids?"

title: "How Did Scientists Discover a Pac-Man Enzyme That Gobbles Plastic?"
excerpt: "Scientists have found a special enzyme — nicknamed the 'Pac-Man enzyme' — that bacteria use to chew through plastic. The discovery shows how nature is already fighting pollution, one tiny bite at a time."

title: "When did Mount Vesuvius really erupt — and how do pomegranates help us find out?"
excerpt: "For almost 2,000 years, everyone agreed: Mount Vesuvius erupted on August 24, AD 79. But fresh clues — from pomegranate seeds to ancient coins — suggest that date might be wrong by months. How do archaeologists unwrap a mystery buried in ash?"

excerpt: "An amateur astronomer searching satellite maps for a camping spot in Quebec noticed a suspiciously round circle on the landscape. excerpt: "Was Van Gogh's swirling sky just imagination? A new study used star-mapping maths to match the painting to a real pre-dawn sky over southern France on July 22, 1889."

title: "How Scientists Are Protecting Wheat, Rice, and Barley From a Hidden Fungus"
excerpt: "Scientists in the UK and Japan have discovered how to strengthen the natural immune defenses of wheat, rice, and barley — three of the world's most important food crops — so they can fight back against a destructive fungus that threatens global food security."

title: "How a Giant Bridge Over the Highway Is Letting Colorado's Wildlife Cross Safely"
excerpt: "A 200-foot-wide wildlife overpass spanning Interstate 25 in Colorado has cut animal-vehicle collisions by 91% in its first 10 months — proving that when we build bridges for nature, everyone wins."

title: "How did Giovanni Cassini spot Saturn's 'yin-yang' moon Iapetus 355 years ago?"
excerpt: "On October 25, 1671, Italian astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovered Iapetus, Saturn's peculiar moon with one half as dark as night and the other as bright as snow. title: "How did X-ray scientists discover that uranium crystals can survive for decades underground?"

title: "5. How Did a 700-Year-Old Chinese Mural End Up at the Met — and Why Did a Chinese Art Institute Spend 3 Years Copying It?"

title: "How did a 2,500-year-old king earn the world's first human rights badge?"
excerpt: "A 29-foot bronze statue of Cyrus the Great now stands in Atlanta's Pardis Park, honoring the ancient Persian king historians call the world's first champion of human rights."

title: "Europe's ExoMars Reaches Mars: The Orbiter That Survived and the Lander That Fell"
excerpt: "On October 19, 2016, the European Space Agency's ExoMars mission touched down at the Red Planet. The Trace Gas Orbiter went into orbit, while the Schiaparelli lander's attempt to land ended in a dramatic crash."

title: Could the first exomoon be hiding in a strange star system far away?
excerpt: Astronomers using the Very Large Telescope in Chile may have spotted the first moon beyond our Solar System — but it's not orbiting a planet. title: "What are the five spooky Halloween skywatching targets this October?"

title: "How does a hidden protein switch turn cells into fat-burning machines?"

title: "The Moon That Looks Like Yin-Yang: How Cassini Discovered Iapetus"
excerpt: "On October 25, 1671, Italian astronomer Giovanni Cassini spotted a strange, shiny speck near Saturn. It turned out to be Iapetus — a moon so oddly half-dark and half-bright that astronomers still call it Saturn's 'yin-yang' moon."

title: "How did scientists find a soil compound that kills bad gut bacteria without harming the good ones?"
excerpt: "Scientists discovered that argyrin B, a compound made by soil-dwelling myxobacteria, can selectively kill harmful gut bacteria while sparing the beneficial microbes that keep our digestion healthy — a major step toward more targeted antibiotics."

title: "What makes a narwhal's tusk twist like a double helix?"

title: "How do rare Moon rocks that fall from space fill gaps in our story of the Moon?"
excerpt: "Some of the best Moon rocks never came from a spacecraft — they are meteorites that were blasted off our nearest neighbor eons ago and rained down on Earth, bringing us pieces of the Moon we never visited."

title: "What are HawkEye 360's signal-hunting satellites, and how does Rocket Lab put them in orbit?"

title: "How did seabirds bounce back on the Isle of Man — and why are sewage and storms still a challenge?"

title: "How does growing plants in space help us care for Earth?"
excerpt: "NASA astronaut Luke Delaney is busy tending to plants aboard the International Space Station, testing how microgravity changes the way life grows — and what that tells us about tending our own planet from up above."

title: "Why do tropical trees breathe at night — and how does it help them survive drought?"

title: "What is Jio Platforms' record-breaking IPO in India?"

title: "Can a clever machine clean toxic algae from our lakes before it makes us sick?"
excerpt: "Hot summer weather turns some lakes green and pea-soup thick with toxic blue-green algae. Now a scientist's idea — born after watching his own child's favorite park close — could give nature a hand."

title: "What Do Flare Ribbons Tell Us About the Sun's Hidden Explosions?"
excerpt: "Solar flares are among the Sun's most powerful explosions, but they happen behind the Sun's bright glare. Scientists are now using flare ribbons — glowing streaks that act like a flare's footprints — to see what these explosions really look like."

title: "How a ghostly, eyeless snail learned to live in a dark Chinese cave"
excerpt: "Deep inside a limestone cave in southern China, scientists found a tiny, see-through snail that has never needed eyes — it has lived its whole life in complete darkness, surviving on diatoms and the faint glow of underground rock."

excerpt: A balloon-borne telescope called Sunrise-III floated 35 km above Earth in 2024 and revealed that even the Sun's "quiet" regions are laced with a surprisingly intricate web of magnetic threads — not the smooth, simple canopy scientists expected.

title: "Why are some monkey brains smooth instead of wrinkly — and what it teaches us about our own?"
excerpt: "Common marmosets are tiny monkeys with almost perfectly smooth brains.
